{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-in-s","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"1b540e40e769577a1a6c251003148ed6cd7f57846cda7c10c03d252786d8c7f2","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-in-class-std:lineage:37","source_registry_sha256":"2800087d52ca58455ac6dac735a6e1bd60a4442f9e09c2356d96bd9ed8102504","source_liveness_sha256":"4d2b75b9a10fb774f53fb2d906a3a7a7f75f5e9387f8b4ddcd423e9b7828d59b"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Accident and emergency confusables and continuation","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: what to hit, when to move the car, vent settings, blowout versus brake failure, and continuation facts on water escapes, roadside kits, theft, night stops and officer conduct","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: what to hit, when to move the car, vent settings, blowout versus brake failure, and continuation facts on water escapes, roadside kits, theft, night stops and officer conduct
Confusable pairs from the accidents and emergencies chapter, followed by continuation facts the main list did not hold; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec09-R01 | anchor: A01
Hitting something moving your way beats hitting something standing still, but hitting something standing still beats a head-on crash, and a sideswipe can help you slow down. [A01]
Why it matters: group collision avoidance; confusable ranking of impacts.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-R02 | anchor: A01
A crash on the traveled highway is normally moved off the road, but a crash with hazardous materials, injury, death or entrapment stays where it is. [A01]
Why it matters: group crash duties; confusable move versus leave.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-R03 | anchor: A05
The fresh-air vent should be closed in congested traffic, yet opened when driving on highways in cold weather. [A05]
Why it matters: group carbon monoxide; confusable vent settings.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec09-R04 | anchor: A03
In a blowout you avoid the brakes until the car is nearly stopped, while in brake failure you pump the pedal hard to build pressure. [A03]
Why it matters: group equipment failures; confusable blowout versus brake failure.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-R05 | anchor: A01
Crashes are often caused by a driver's inattention, failure to follow the rules of the road, or both. [A01]
Why it matters: group crash causes; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-R06 | anchor: A02
Pulling back onto the pavement too quickly after drifting onto the shoulder can throw the vehicle off balance. [A02]
Why it matters: group shoulder recovery; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-R07 | anchor: A02
Power windows usually still open after a car enters water unless the impact damaged the electrical system. [A02]
Why it matters: group car in water; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-R08 | anchor: A02
In a car in water, have older children help younger ones and move passengers to the front seats as calmly as possible. [A02]
Why it matters: group car in water; sequence item.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-R09 | anchor: A02
Riding on the roof of a car in water keeps you as dry as possible, and swimming for shore is a last resort if help has not come before the car sinks. [A02]
Why it matters: group car in water; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-R10 | anchor: A02
Other warning signs of an impaired driver include swerving or drifting, following too closely, abrupt or illegal turns and inconsistent signaling. [A02]
Why it matters: group impaired drivers; continuation of the list.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-R11 | anchor: A03
The manual's roadside emergency tips are safety guidelines that are not necessarily required by Indiana law. [A03]
Why it matters: group roadside emergencies; scope note.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-R12 | anchor: A03
Keep a flashlight with fresh batteries within the driver's reach, plus a reflective safety vest and a red reflective triangle in the vehicle. [A03]
Why it matters: group roadside emergencies; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-R13 | anchor: A03
In winter, pack blankets, extra gloves and warm hats in case you must wait for responders or a tow. [A03]
Why it matters: group roadside emergencies; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-R14 | anchor: A03
Do not try to switch off the vehicle while it is still moving in a highway emergency. [A03]
Why it matters: group ignition; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-R15 | anchor: A03
Parking with the front wheels turned sharply right and the emergency brake set helps prevent theft, as can an anti-theft device. [A03]
Why it matters: group theft; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-R16 | anchor: A03
If you do not turn on your signal when an officer pulls you over, the officer may think you are avoiding the stop or are impaired. [A03]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-R17 | anchor: A04
If stopped at night, look for a well-lit place such as near street lights, restaurants or service stations, and consider turning on the interior light. [A04]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec09-R18 | anchor: A04
If your windows are tinted, roll them all down after stopping and before the officer reaches you. [A04]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec09-R19 | anchor: A04
A driver suspected of drunk driving who refuses breath, urine, blood or performance tests can lose driving privileges. [A04]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; link to chemical test suspensions.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec09-R20 | anchor: A04
Officers must give their names and badge numbers on request, and misconduct can be reported to their superiors, internal affairs or a civilian complaint board. [A04]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec09-R21 | anchor: A04
Police are legally required to document every traffic stop, including the driver's name and address. [A04]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec09-R22 | anchor: A05
Symptoms of carbon monoxide poisoning can include drowsiness or dizziness, bluish skin or lips, headache and increased sensitivity to light. [A05]
Why it matters: group carbon monoxide; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec09-R23 | anchor: A05
A faulty exhaust can leak fumes into the back seat, so have the exhaust checked regularly and listen for any unusual roar under the car. [A05]
Why it matters: group carbon monoxide; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0067]
